doc.citation: Wellman, C. H. (2024). Spore assemblages from the Silurian-Lower Devonian ‘Lower Old Red Sandstone’ deposits of the Lanark Basin of the Midland Valley of Scotland. Fossil Imprint, 80(1): 9–18.
doc.comment: Fish Bed Formation records update assemblages previously described by Wellman and Richardson (1993), Terrestrial plant microfossils from Silurian inliers of the Midland Valley of Scotland. Table 1 provides a pooled formation-level list; the Appendix lists 43 samples, including 13 marked barren. The pooled record and its constituent sample records overlap and must not be counted as independent assemblages. Sample occurrence lists contain only taxa linked by figure captions; empty lists do not imply absence unless explicitly stated. Greywacke Conglomerate Formation records represent one new sample. Table–caption naming differences and additional illustrated morphotypes are retained or flagged; these should not be summed as independent taxa. Grid references are preserved in notes without conversion.

items.age_basis_detail: CN chulus-nanus Spore Assemblage Biozone, citing Richardson and McGregor (1986) and Burgess and Richardson (1991, 1995).
items.notes: Pooled Table 1 list, not a sample-by-taxon matrix. Appendix contains 43 samples: 13 barren and 30 with preservation or assemblage descriptions. Rich palynological assemblages also contain freshwater phytoplankton, phytodebris and animal remains, excluded from occurrences. Material includes assemblages previously described by Wellman and Richardson (1993). Formation-level record overlaps the constituent sample records below.
items.locator: Spore assemblages from the Fish Bed Formation, pp. 11–13; Table 1; Text-figs 3–5; Appendix, p. 18

items.locality: A70 road near Glenbuck Loch, Lanark Basin, Midland Valley of Scotland
items.depth_or_level: a thin impersistent dark green shale unit in a coarse sandstone layer immediately above the contact with the Quarry Arenite
items.age_as_reported: Early Devonian Lochkovian age (early, but not earliest to late, but not latest Lochkovian)
items.age_basis_detail: Primary assignment to the micrornatus-newportensis Spore Assemblage Biozone from the spores; supporting regional radiometric ages from associated volcanic/intrusive rocks reported by Thirlwall (1988): Pentland Hills Volcanic Fm Rb/Sr phenocryst biotite 412.6 ± 5.7 Ma; Tinto Felsite Sm-Nd garnet ca. 411.9 ± 1.9 Ma and Rb-Sr biotite 407.2 ± 6.7 Ma. These are not dates measured on the sampled shale.
items.setting_as_reported: alluvial fans, sourced from the Southern Uplands, and deposited in an arid-semi arid environment
items.notes: Sample 21CW053-21SCOT08; illustrated slides 21SCOT08.1 and 21SCOT08.2. Grid Reference HS75514/28543 is retained exactly as printed. Assemblage described as depauperate, with 16 types in Table 2, low yield and probable size sorting that removed smaller elements. Preparation contains only land-derived spores and phytodebris. Emphanisporites sp. in Table 2 and Emphanisporites ?micrornatus spp. in the caption are overlapping identifications, not independent taxa; the prose calls the latter Emphanisporites ?micrornatus and reports a single specimen. Text-fig. 6b prints Retusotriletus triangulatus, whereas Table 2 and Text-fig. 6f print Retusotriletes triangulatus; the table spelling is used here. Reticulate spore is captioned Reticulate ?trilete spore. Verrucate spore caption records may overlap Verrucosisporites sp. or other table morphotypes, but equivalence is not stated. Caption-only morphotypes and Aneurospora spp. are included. Text-fig. 7 tetrads are described as trilete-spore tetrads, not identified as obligate cryptospore tetrads. Its spore mass is an additional non-taxonomic observation.
items.locator: Material and methods, p. 10; Table 2 and Spore Assemblage from the Greywacke Conglomerate Formation, p. 13; Discussion, p. 13; Text-figs 6–7, pp. 16–17
